name: Gad
bio:
Gad was a prophet, later known as "David's seer." While David had brought his parents to Mizpah in Moab for safety and was himself hiding in a stronghold, the prophet Gad told him, "Do not stay in the stronghold. Go into the land of Judah," and David obeyed, going to the forest of Hereth (1 Samuel 22:5). Gad went on to play an important role throughout David's life as one who conveyed the LORD's word to him, a story that continues through the rest of 1 and 2 Samuel.

Years later, after David took a census of Israel and Judah against Joab's advice, his conscience struck him and he confessed his sin to the LORD. The LORD sent Gad to offer David a choice of three punishments: seven years of famine, three months of fleeing from enemies, or three days of plague. David chose to fall into the LORD's hands rather than human hands, and a devastating plague struck Israel, killing seventy thousand before the LORD relented at Jerusalem. Gad then instructed David to build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite, which David did, ending the plague (2 Samuel 24:10-25).
